stem: Two cards are drawn simultaneously from a well-shuffled standard deck of 52 cards. What is the probability that both cards are kings?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Treats the two draws as independent: (4/52) x (4/52) = 16/2704 = 1/169. This ignores the without-replacement condition.
Computes 6/1326 but incorrectly simplifies to 2/221 instead of 1/221 (off by factor 2).
Uses P = 4/52 treating it as a single draw probability, not accounting for drawing two cards simultaneously.

explanation: Two cards are drawn simultaneously (without replacement). This is a combinations problem. Favourable outcomes: choosing 2 kings from 4 available = C(4,2) = 6. Total outcomes: choosing any 2 cards from 52 = C(52,2) = 52x51/2 = 1326. P = 6/1326 = 1/221.

explanation_sections.approach: Identify model: classical probability with combinations (simultaneous draw = without replacement, unordered). Numerator: C(4,2) = 6. Denominator: C(52,2) = 1326. Divide and reduce: 6/1326 = 1/221.
explanation_sections.lesson: Simultaneous draws require combinations. The independence trap (squaring single-draw probability) gives a wrong answer because it treats replacement as happening between draws.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. Know C(52,2)=1326, C(4,2)=6 by memory. Spot the independence trap at option 1.
